newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 17.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.
- Ireland's Deputy Prime Minister Dick Spring has a maximum of six weeks in the run-up to the general election to reverse a slump in support for his Labour Party in the greater Dublin area.

- Ireland's Cityjet has announced it will begin direct scheduled flights from Dublin to Paris on May 1, thus intensifying the already competitive market for passengers between both capitals. - The level of the Irihs pound appears to be the main factor determining Irish inflation but excessive wage demands also play a part, according to research by two economists at Ireland's Central Bank.
- Ireland's Enterprise and Employment Minister Richard Bruton is seeking legal advice as his officials try to prepare legislation to ban below-cost selling by imported newspapers.

- The Irish Ambassador to China, Joe Hayes, has been called in by the Chinese Foreign Ministry to be informed of Beijing's displeasure at Ireland's co-sponsorship of a Danish UN resolution condemning China's human rights records. - The triple killer discovered living in Cork, southern Ireland, consented to his extradition to Britain on Wednesday after telling a court he was confident of being released from detention there.

- Republic of Ireland manager Mick McCarthy refused to confirm that Paul McGrath's career with the Irish international football team was finished as he omitted him from the squad for the World Cup Group Eight qualifier against Romania on April 30. - The board of Waterford Foods Plc will on Thursday consider the terms of the proposed merger with Avonmore, which would create a 2.5 billion Irish pound dairy and meat group.

- Britain's Home Office was on Wednesday called on to explain why it took over a year to file extradition proceedings against triple-killer Alan Reeve, amid reports from senior Irish police that the British were not interested in extraditing him from Ireland.
- The Irish stock market index is expected to rise by 7.5 percent to 3,250 by the end of the year.
